_comment: MCP server config loaded by the `claude` CLI in agent/Dockerfile's image (see docker-compose.yml `agent` service, --mcp-config). Plain JSON has no comment syntax, so notes live in these _comment keys instead — the `claude` CLI ignores unknown keys, and the sibling Jobs project's docker/mcp.json (heavily-commented everywhere else) is itself comment-free, evidence the same convention already held there. ${VAR:-default} below is Claude Code's documented env-var expansion for .mcp.json; it reads this container's actual environment (docker-compose.yml `agent` service), so it stays correct if either default ever changes there.

truthcv._comment: TruthCV's own tool surface: generate_cover_letter, record_application, record_screening, check_cooldown, get_canonical_cv, get_profile_answers, record_company_board, get_job_profiles, recommend_salary (mcp/server.py, APIRouter(prefix='/mcp')). The default is the in-network address of the `app` compose service — reachable only from inside the compose network, not from the host or the open internet.

browser._comment: The agent's browser driver: @playwright/mcp serving headful Chromium under Xvfb in the `browser` compose service (browser/Dockerfile, browser/entrypoint.sh). Exposes browser_navigate, browser_click, browser_type, browser_file_upload, browser_snapshot, browser_take_screenshot and the rest of the upstream Playwright MCP tool set, which is why agent/daily-apply.sh grants the whole server as `mcp__browser` rather than enumerating tools. The default is the in-network address of the `browser` service — reachable only from inside the compose network, not from the host or the open internet. The container keeps a persistent Chromium profile on a named volume, so a one-time manual login through the noVNC viewport at http://localhost:7900 survives restarts, and it mounts the app data volume read-only at /app/data so browser_file_upload can resolve the `path` get_canonical_cv returns.

_fallbackComment: HISTORY, so the retired design is not reinstated by mistake: the ORIGINAL plan was to drive the operator's real, already-logged-in HOST Chrome through an `interceptor` daemon over a bind-mounted unix socket, with a containerised Playwright browser as the documented fallback. That primary path never existed as software — neither this repo nor the retiring Jobs repo contains an interceptor MCP server or its launch command; Jobs merely allow-listed mcp__interceptor__interceptor_{browser,read,local} against a server declared in the operator's personal Claude config, plus a Chrome extension its own docs record as NOT INSTALLED as of 2026-08-12. So the agent had no working browser driver at all. The containerised browser above replaced it: it is a real, running MCP server, it keeps its sessions on a persistent profile volume, and it lives in its own container so a browser crash cannot take the agent loop down. Logged-in ATS/SSO sessions are established once through the noVNC viewport instead of inherited from the host.
